renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: cancer_intron_manhattan
  title: Cancer intron candidates along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a junction that matched the CTAT cancer intron reference, placed at its start, with the number of uniquely mapped reads that support it, coloured by the TCGA cohort where it is most prevalent. It answers which candidate cancer introns the run holds and how strongly they are read.
    How to read: a tall point is a cancer-associated intron seen in many reads, the best candidate to follow up. Colour by chromosome or strand from the controls to see where the candidates cluster.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the support values of this table, a reference the data defines itself. CTAT requires at least 5 read alignments for an intron to enter its reference, which is a rule of the reference build and not of this sample, so it is not drawn here.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: Uniquely mapped reads
    top_n_labels: 6
    color_by_columns:
    - top_tcga_cohort
    - strand
    default_color_by: top_tcga_cohort
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: start
    score: score
    feature: gene

- component: card
  title: Reads per cancer intron
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of uniquely mapped reads supporting a candidate intron, and the histogram shows how the counts are distributed. It answers how well supported the candidates are.
    How to read: candidates resting on one or two reads are fragile and need confirmation in the arc view. Strongly supported ones are the leads to follow.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md
  column: uniq_mapped
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: reads per junction, distribution

- component: card
  title: Cancer intron candidates
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct introns that matched the CTAT cancer intron reference, and the bars rank the TCGA cohorts where those introns are most prevalent. It answers how many cancer-associated junctions the run holds and in which tumour types they are common.
    How to read: a run with no candidates gives an empty tile, which is normal. A cohort leading the ranking hints at the tumour type the sample resembles, but a single intron says little on its own.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md
  column: intron
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: top_tcga_cohort
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: TCGA cohorts holding the most candidates
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Prevalence in the leading TCGA cohort
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest prevalence, in percent of the tumours of its cohort, reached by a candidate intron, and the histogram shows how the prevalences are distributed. It answers how common the candidates are in the tumours where they were seen.
    How to read: a high prevalence marks an intron frequent in a tumour type, which makes it a recurrent event. Low values are rare events.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md
  column: top_tcga_pct
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: prevalence in the leading cohort, distribution

- component: table
  title: Cancer intron candidates
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate intron, with its position, gene, supporting reads and its prevalence in TCGA tumour cohorts and GTEx normal tissues. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile.
    How to read: a high TCGA prevalence with a low GTEx prevalence marks an intron specific to tumours, the pattern CTAT-SPLICING looks for.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md

- component: advanced_viz
  id: junction_arcs
  title: Splice junctions as arcs
  description: |-
    Each arc is one splice junction, from its donor to its acceptor, with the number of uniquely mapped reads printed at its apex, and one lane per sample. It answers which introns the reads of a locus use and how strongly.
    How to read: a strong arc is a well supported intron, and a weak arc beside it is an alternative junction worth a look when it skips or extends an exon. Compare lanes to see whether a junction is shared between samples.
    Note: the exon support drawn under the arcs is inferred from the junction ends and the reads that touch them, it is not a coverage measurement.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/TrinityCTAT/CTAT-SPLICING/Home.md
  kind: sashimi
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    count: uniq_mapped
    sample: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: intron_manhattan
  title: Junction support along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a splice junction, placed at its start, with the number of uniquely mapped reads that support it, coloured by chromosome. It answers where along the genome the best supported junctions lie.
    How to read: tall points are junctions seen in many reads, usually canonical introns of highly expressed genes. A tall point in an unexpected gene is a junction to check in the arc view.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the support values of this table, a reference the data defines itself and not a cut-off published by CTAT-SPLICING. The labelled points are the strongest junctions.
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: Uniquely mapped reads
    top_n_labels: 6
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: start
    score: score
    feature: gene

- component: figure
  title: Junction reads per gene
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene, with the uniquely mapped reads of its splice junctions added up and coloured by strand. It answers which genes carry the most junction reads.
    How to read: a tall bar is a highly expressed gene or one with many junctions. Bars are split by strand, so a gene read on both strands stands out.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: gene
    y: uniq_mapped
    color: strand
    labels:
      gene: Gene
      uniq_mapped: Uniquely mapped reads
      strand: Strand

- component: card
  title: Reads per junction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of uniquely mapped reads supporting a junction, and the histogram shows how the counts are distributed. It answers how well supported a typical junction is.
    How to read: read support is heavily skewed, with many weakly supported junctions and a few very strong ones. A median near the floor means most junctions rest on very few reads and are fragile calls.
  column: uniq_mapped
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: reads per junction, distribution

- component: card
  title: Distinct junctions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct introns seen, and the bars rank the genes by how many distinct junctions each carries. It answers how many junctions the run found and where they cluster.
    How to read: a gene with many junctions is long or has many isoforms. Count and distinct count differ when the same intron appears in several samples.
  column: intron
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: genes with the most distinct junctions

- component: card
  title: Junction reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is every read supporting a junction, unique and multi mapped, and the ring splits it by chromosome. It answers how the junction reads divide between chromosomes.
    How to read: a chromosome with a large share is gene dense or holds a very expressed gene. Multi mapped reads are included, so repeated loci weigh in.
  column: total_mapped
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: chrom
  caption: junction reads, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Intron length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median length of an intron in bases, and the histogram shows how lengths are distributed. It answers how long the spliced introns are.
    How to read: lengths span orders of magnitude, so the median is more telling than the mean. Very short introns can be spurious alignments, and a long tail holds the introns of large genes.
  column: intron_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: intron length, distribution

- component: table
  title: Splice junctions
  description: |-
    Each row is a splice junction, with its position, length, strand, gene and the unique, multi mapped and total reads that support it. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by reads to find the best supported junctions, or filter by gene to list its introns.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene
